title: An imported part with no bin location goes to an Unassigned bin
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at a location that has no bin location named Unassigned.
  • Use part numbers for two new parts, part A and part B, that no part or Part Library entry uses yet.
  • Have a parts import file with two rows that add part A and part B, each with quantity 0 and an empty bin location cell.
  • Start on that location's Inventory data import page (Settings, then Data Import, then Inventory).
custom_steps:
1. Upload the file.
  2. Run the import.
  3. Click Bin Locations under Parts in the Settings menu.
  4. Click Parts in the top bar.
  5. Click Inventory in the left menu.
  6. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  7. Click the part A row.
  8. Click Cancel.
  9. Type part B's part number in the Search box.
  10. Click the part B row.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The file is ready to import.

Step 2:

  • The import finishes and adds both parts.

Step 3:

  • The Bin Locations list holds exactly one bin location named "Unassigned" (0 before + 1 made by the import = 1).

Step 4:

  • The Parts left menu shows Inventory.

Step 5:

  • The Inventory page opens.

Step 6:

  • Part A is listed, and its Bin Location / Quantity cell shows Unassigned with 0.
  • Its Total Qty shows 0 Available, a quantity and not "Not Tracked": the import added part A as a tracked part.

Step 7:

  • The window shows the Track quantities and cost of goods switch on.
  • The Inventory section of the window shows one bin row: Bin Location "Unassigned", Quantity 0, marked Default.

Step 8:

  • The window closes.

Step 9:

  • Part B is listed, with 0 Available in Total Qty.

Step 10:

  • Part B also shows the switch on and one bin row: Bin Location "Unassigned", Quantity 0, marked Default.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description)

  • S7-N10: “An import row that adds a tracked part with no bin location puts the part in a bin named "Unassigned", which the import creates at the location if it is missing. On a new part that bin is the default bin.”
  • S7-N11: “A part the import adds is tracked. The import has no tracking column and never changes an existing part's tracking. The import template's "name" column is the part's description.”

From: Product's answers (Chris Ward, 9 Oct and 14 Oct 2026, saved in po-answers-2026-10-09/ and po-answers-2026-10-14/), read 27 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 3 a) of 14 Oct 2026: “The part goes into a bin named "Unassigned", which the import creates if it's missing. On a new part that bin is the default (S7-N10).”

From: Product's answers to questions 13 to 27 (Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, Google Doc https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pkAPGqWVTdtYorNN4SVNl9HkHxuuB9czro_y2DbUeEM/edit, saved word for word in full-pass-2026-10-27/ANSWERS-13-27-2026-10-27.md), read 28 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, answer 16: “(a) Tracked. The import has no tracking column, and it never changes an existing part's tracking. (b) Yes, the "name" column is the part's description (S7-N11).”
  • Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, answer 17: “Settings. The path is Settings → Parts → Bin Locations (S5-E2). Roles & Permissions is also under Settings (S12-R6).”
